member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.Language.Json.Syntax.InternalSyntax.Blender
member.summary: Offers the parser pieces of the previous tree that the edit did not touch.

remarks.para: The rule that keeps this honest is that the parser is always driven by the lexer. A position only moves because a token was really read out of the new text, or because a node was adopted whose text is known to match. Nothing is worked out by arithmetic alone.

That matters more than it sounds. Type a single quote in the middle of a document and the lexer reads one unterminated string running to the end of the file; it never again stops where an old node began, so nothing after the quote is offered. A blender that trusted its own sums would happily reuse all of it and produce a tree that does not match its own text.

member.summary: Builds the immutable tree for a JSON document, keeping every character of it.

remarks.para: Whatever the text says, the tree reproduces it exactly and parsing finishes. Both follow from one rule: a value knows what can follow it. is told which tokens end the construct it sits in, and skips everything up to the first of them, so it always consumes something unless it is already looking at one. Each loop then excludes exactly the tokens it passes down, which is why none of them can spin.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Language.Json.Syntax.InternalSyntax.LanguageParser.MaxDepth
member.summary: How deeply objects and arrays may nest before the rest is kept as skipped text.
member.remarks: The parser follows the shape of the document with its own call stack, so without a limit a deeply enough nested document would end the process instead of reporting anything. The limit is far above anything a document written to be read reaches, and well below the depth at which the stack runs out.
